notes: The supplied PNGs are only 256x192 and stored rotated 90 degrees. I rotated every frame upright, upscaled 4x, and made further zoomed crops before judging. Everything is soft and motion-blurred, which is why several counts are marked probable/unsure rather than certain.

Number of brown sofas: I report 2. Frames 01-04 show a brown suede sofa carrying a grey pom-pom throw and two dark grey cushions, with the dining/patio end behind it. Frames 10-13 show a brown suede sofa of the same family with a navy and a cream cushion and no throw, backing onto the staircase. The whole scan spans only about 140 seconds, so the throw could not have been moved between them; I read them as a two-piece suite. If they are in fact one sofa, the count drops to 1.

The scan is an open-plan space. Through a wide opening (frames 03-04) a kitchen/dining area is visible - dining table, white chairs, tulips, kitchen counter, a row of small prints; and through a doorway (frame 17) a bedroom - bed, bedside cabinet, framed picture. I listed those items but they are strictly in adjoining spaces, not in the living room itself.

In frame 08 there are two small dark objects on the white sideboard. One is clearly a slim remote control; the second has a bent, hinged outline and may be a folded pair of glasses rather than a second remote.

The dark object on the floor at the right edge of frame 03 may be the same black pet bed that is clearly visible in frame 04, seen from the opposite direction, rather than a separate bag. Its outline looked rounded to me, so I kept it under 'bag' and did not add frame 03 to the pet bed.

Display cabinets: the tall four-pane cabinet by the stairs (frames 09, 12, 13) and the lower cabinet with a wood-framed glass door near the dining end (frame 03) look like different pieces, but I never see both in one frame, so the count of 2 is unsure.

There are two different wood-holding items: a brass/steel wire basket lying by the hearth (frame 07) and a black metal rack with logs by the sideboard (frame 08). I listed them as separate objects rather than merging them into one 'log basket' with count 2.

Rug count is unsure. Frames 03/04/10/12 could all be showing one pale grey rug in the seating area seen from different angles; the dark teal rug with gold motifs in frame 07 is definitely a second, separate one.

Frames 05 and 06 (two windows, roman blinds, radiators, palm, snake plant, cactus, elephant ornament) share the same floor and wall finish as the rest of the scan, but no frame links them geometrically to the sofa/TV area, so I cannot confirm they are the same room rather than a directly adjoining part of the same open space.

Framed pictures are numerous and mostly small and blurred; the count of 12 is my best tally of physically distinct frames across all views and could easily be off by two or three, mainly in the row on the dining-area wall.
I deliberately did not list purely architectural surfaces (white brick feature wall, charcoal painted wall panel, wood-look flooring, ceiling) as objects, though they are clearly visible.
The picnic table and bench visible through the patio door in frames 01-02 are outdoors and are not included in the object list.
